title: Reduction Trace Semantics

basis.scope: Canonical reduction trace semantics for REDUCE_025 outputs, including trace-step records, halt reasons, and outcome-linked diagnostic records.

core_rule.statement: Trace(C) is a diagnostic record, not a continuation; every REDUCE_025 result carries a trace; trace steps preserve the distinction between NF(C), pNF(C), and classified ⊥C_x; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the canonical reduction trace object produced by REDUCE_025, so every reduction outcome records the lawful sequence by which it was reached.

canonical_claims.statement: Every REDUCE_025 result must have a trace.
Trace(C) is diagnostic, not a continuation.
Trace(C) preserves the distinction between NF(C), pNF(C), and continuation failure.
Trace(C) may record failure, but failure remains non-continuational.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Trace
formal_objects.definition: The ordered diagnostic record of the evaluation, validation, lawful reduction, halt, and failure-classification steps applied to a continuation expression C during REDUCE_025.

formal_objects.name: Trace Step
formal_objects.definition: A single evaluation, validation, reduction, halt, or failure-classification event within Trace(C).

invariants: Trace(C) is diagnostic, not a continuation.
Trace(C) does not modify reduction semantics.
Every REDUCE_025 result must have a trace.
Trace(C) preserves the distinction between NF(C), pNF(C), and ⊥C_x.
Trace(C) may record failure, but failure remains non-continuational.

next_recommended_patch.title: Reduction Trace Equivalence
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Define when two reduction traces are equivalent despite differing reduction paths, provided they preserve lawful continuation semantics and identical reduction outcomes.
